stories.headline: Karis state visit to Finland triggers domestic controversy over Russia dialogue remarks
stories.summary: President Alar Karis made a two-day state visit to Finland on April 28–29, during which he and Finnish President Stubb held a joint press conference and addressed defence cooperation and the war in Ukraine. Karis's statements — that Europe made a strategic mistake by not pursuing peace talks with Russia in spring 2022, and that dialogue with Moscow must eventually resume — drew sharp criticism from Foreign Minister Tsahkna, Social Democrats leader Läänemets, and other politicians, sparking the week's dominant domestic political debate. Karis defended his position in a Vikerraadio interview, arguing his remarks had been misread; Tsahkna publicly stated the president's position contradicts Estonian foreign policy.

stories.headline: Tsahkna chairs NB8 meeting in Kuressaare, pushes 21st EU sanctions package and EU enlargement
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna convened the Nordic-Baltic Eight (NB8) foreign ministers meeting in Kuressaare Castle with EU High Representative Kaja Kallas, discussing Ukraine support, EU enlargement, and transatlantic relations. In parallel, Tsahkna met Lithuania's FM Budrys on EU enlargement, announced Estonia's position on a tougher 21st EU sanctions package targeting Russian energy, and made statements on press freedom and diaspora policy. Estonia separately confirmed it will deny airspace access to flights attending Russia's May 9 parade.

stories.headline: EKRE nominates Mart Helme as its presidential candidate for autumn 2026 election
stories.summary: The Conservative People's Party (EKRE) council convened on May 1 and nominated founding member and former party chair Mart Helme as its presidential candidate, pending confirmation by the party congress in one month. EKRE leader Martin Helme said the party aims to 'conquer Kadriorg,' and Mart Helme emphasised nation, family, and home as his key values, positioning himself as distinct from the current government's foreign policy line.

stories.headline: Government approves drone defence legislation and law allowing allied forces in hybrid threat response
stories.summary: The Estonian government approved two defence-related bills on the same week: a drone regulation expanding rights for the military, police, and critical infrastructure operators to counter drone threats, backed by PM Michal; and a separate amendment to the Defence Forces Organisation Act allowing allied forces to be called in to assist with border protection and public order during hybrid incidents such as 'little green men' scenarios, backed by Defence Minister Pevkur.

stories.headline: Pevkur's defence diplomacy week: Finland meeting, Locked Shields, US equipment delay commentary
stories.summary: Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur had a working visit to Finland where he met Finnish Defence Minister Häkkänen, coinciding with President Karis's state visit. Pevkur also represented Estonia at the NATO Locked Shields cyber exercise, where he highlighted growing cyber threat complexity. Separately, Pevkur was quoted in multiple international outlets acknowledging that US defence equipment deliveries to Europe are delayed due to the Middle East conflict, while expressing confidence in the overall alliance.

stories.headline: 2025 public sector salary data published: Karis and Kõve top earners; cabinet salaries disclosed
stories.summary: Estonia's Finance Ministry released 2025 public sector salary data, showing President Karis and Supreme Court Chief Justice Kõve as the highest earners at €115,118 each — the first time presidential pay exceeded €10,000 per month. A separate table published ministerial and adviser salaries, with PM Michal as the top earner in cabinet at over €100,000 annually.

stories.headline: Estonian banking and economy: Q1 GDP up 1.3%, housing loans at decade-best margin, bank Q1 results
stories.summary: Swedbank and SEB published analyses showing Estonian GDP grew 1.3% year-on-year in Q1 2026, with the housing loan market more active than the same period in 2025 and mortgage margins at a ten-year low of 1.4%. Artea Pank (formerly Bigbank) reported Q1 net profit of €15.4m, down 13% year-on-year. Coop Pank disclosed routine share buyback transactions. The ECB's April 30 monetary policy decision — a rate cut — was published in Estonian.
